summary: Independent weak-signal pass confirms XTND is a legitimate newly public robotics challenger but finds a material capital-structure/dilution question that must be resolved before admission. The registered sensor mesh also exposes a broader blind spot: Earth currently has no explicit causal node/metric for commercial-space regulatory throughput even though FAA licensing policy is becoming a first-order capacity constraint/accelerant. Acquisition is incomplete because the full cadence-due sensor set could not be exhaustively queried in this run; sensor gaps are recorded as unknowns and do not alter gating coverage.

materialFindings.finding: XTND remains a credible outside-universe discovery, but its post-merger equity structure requires explicit normalization before methodology admission. A Sept. 4 Form S-8 registers 43,567,442 shares across rollover awards, the 2026 equity plan and ESPP.

Commercial-space licensing throughput is an uncovered 2036 dependency candidate. FAA states all legacy operators transitioned to Part 450 by March 9, 2026 and that one license can cover portfolios of operations/configurations/sites; a July 28 initiative further seeks faster launch/reentry/site approvals. This can change launch cadence, infrastructure utilization and competitive entry barriers, but Earth causal-graph.json currently contains only GEV/grid nodes and no commercial-space regulatory-throughput node.

Sensor-source findings remain non-gating. BIS current EAR material and FTC/FAA sensor observations were reviewed as early-warning inputs only; no score/rank influence is proposed without event normalization, entity resolution and primary corroboration.

proposedCanonicalChanges.proposal: Research and, only after Chief verification, consider adding a causal dependency node for commercial-space regulatory/licensing throughput with measurable FAA license/approval cadence and operator/site exposure; do not alter scores this cycle.
Before XTND admission, normalize fully diluted share count and equity-plan overhang against post-merger shares outstanding and financing needs.

contradictions.issue: Discovery note emphasizes deployment scale and strategic relevance while current discovery state does not surface the unusually large newly registered equity-plan share pool; this is not a contradiction of operating capability but is a missing admission-risk dimension.

unknowns: Exact XTND post-merger basic and fully diluted shares outstanding, cash runway, financing dependence and equity-plan dilution percentage remain unresolved.

Federal Register, OFAC, NIH RePORTER, NSF, NHTSA, EPA ECHO, DOJ, BEA and other cadence-due sensor sweeps were not exhaustively completed in this run; absence of findings is not evidence of absence and does not reduce machine gating coverage.
The economic magnitude of FAA licensing streamlining on specific public companies is not yet quantified.

Whether every registered sensor should be queried every Beta run versus cadence-aware rotation; exhaustive hourly querying may add latency without proportional accuracy gain.
